flags: Overlaps with other categories, records created anyway: knot (ludi entry-286, climbing knot), apron (culina entry-257, praecīnctōrium), handkerchief (domus entry-67), pocket (sermo entry-236, sinus), swim cap (the ludi swimming records). Extended two ludi records, swimsuit and swimming-trunks, which the ludi batch may also touch.

Homonyms elsewhere get a sense and an ID that says which: button-clothes (culina entry-117 has the appliance button, also globulus), collar-garment (natura entry-510 has the dog collar, collāre), warm-clothes (natura entry-502, weather), light-clothes (domus entry-271, electric light).

subūcula: entry-317 calls it the undershirt, as do Traupman 118 (undershirt), M-O s.v. undershirt and Lewis & Short (a man’s under-garment); the existing shirt record recommends it for an ordinary shirt (Mir) and undershirt leads with interula.

Periods: an ancient garment word applied to its nearest modern counterpart is classical, as in the models (paenula coat, tunicula T-shirt, umbella umbrella, fībula safety pin, thōrāx lāneus sweater, vestis muliebris dress); an old word in a different sense is modern or Renaissance (globulus button, ocellus buttonhole, loculus pocket, subligar apron, collāre collar from Comenius, ocreae boots from Erasmus).

The card calls colobium (Servius), amictōrium (Cod. Th.) and coriaceus late; kept late, the later period, though these sources are non-Christian (Lewis & Short cites Amm. for coriaceus, Serv. and Cod. Th. for colobium, Cod. Th. and Hier. for amictōrium), which the scheme would call post-classical.

gossypinus marked modern: Lewis & Short has only gossympinus, i, f., the cotton tree (Plin. 12.39), and Mayhoff’s text (Perseus) reads arborem vocant gossypinum, a tree’s name, not an adjective “of cotton”; check M-O’s citation of Pliny.
camīsula is marked long but camisiola and camisia are not; Lewis & Short prints camĭsĭa (short i), M-O marks all three long (camîsula, camîsiola, camîs(i)a).
digitālia “not in L&S”: Lewis & Short gives digitalibus as a variant reading of Varr. RR 1.55.1 (s.v. digitabulum and digitalis).
lānātus is glossed “woollen” as on the card; Lewis & Short has “furnished with wool, woolly”; Traupman 118 gives lānātus and lānius for woollen.

M-O s.v. swimsuit gives subligar natātōrium for close-fitting, briefs-type swimwear and femōralia natātōria for loose swim trunks; the card cites M-O for subligar balneāre / natātōrium as swimming trunks.

shoelace leads with vincula calceōrum, as the card does (and its example), though corrigia is the classical word (Cic. Div. 2.84; Traupman 117; M-O s.v. shoelace); Lewis & Short also cites vincula of sandal-ties (Verg. A. 8.458; Tib. 1.5.66).

overalls: the card endorses no form; superindūmentum operārium (queried by M-O) leads only because a record needs one, with Traupman’s encombōma in its comment. Skirt has no record, since the card leaves the word open; its remark sits in dress.

Our periods: globulōs stringere (from lexicon-notes-01) and the ratiōnem … reddendam esse descriptions are ours, as the card calls them descriptions, though Cicero uses the arbitrārī construction (Verr. 2.2.28). Later of two possible periods: tunica levior (modern, M-O’s own), ocreae (Renaissance, Erasmus; M-O marks the boot sense medieval, citing Latham).

entry-320’s sources name Gellius and Traupman pp. 38, 317, 334, 404, which no item on the card uses; they match the laundry entry (entry-421). M-O’s safety-pin entry is s.v. safety pin, not sew: safety pin.

chīrothēca: medieval as the card says; the cycling-gloves card (vectura entry-21) calls it post-classical, and it is not in Lewis & Short. calceī altī cummeī: Lewis & Short has only gummeus (Aus.), though it gives cummi as Pliny’s spelling of the noun.

entry-40 split into slack off and idle (“be idle” as a search word), since the card separates shirking (cessō in context, labōrem neglegō, sēgniter agō) from idleness (ōtiō mē dēdō, langueō). The ID is idle, not be-idle: tests/test_convert_cards.py creates its own be-idle record (headword “be idle”) on a copy of the data, and fails if one exists.

Search sees each card’s “See also” labels, and tests/search.browser.test.mjs pins “pyjama” (3 in Vestītus, 6 in all) and “climb” (none in Vestītus): so knot does not relate to the climbing card (entry-286) and dressing gown relates to nightclothes, not pyjamas.

Main records, which take the old links (and the related links of socks, stockings, trousers, shirt, underpants and shoe): button-clothes, cap, sweater, button-up, wear, hood, t-shirt, necklace, cotton, needle, slack-off, accountability. Added related links to tights from socks and stockings, and to shorts and jeans from trousers.
